summary:
Every palindrome has a centre, a letter or a gap between letters. Expand from each of the 2n − 1 centres while
the ends match, and remember the widest expansion (only a strictly longer one replaces it, so the leftmost wins
ties). Return the longest palindrome itself. O(n²) time, O(1) space.

question.md:
Find the longest substring of `s` that reads the same both ways, and return the longest palindrome itself.

- **Single letters** are palindromes, so the answer is at least 1.
- **Ties go to the leftmost** palindrome of the greatest length.
- **n ≤ 2000.**

think.md:
`"xabbaycdcz"` → 'abba'.

Instead of testing substrings, grow palindromes from their middle. From a centre, extending one letter on each
side keeps the palindrome as long as the two new letters match, and the first mismatch means nothing wider at
this centre can work. Even-length palindromes centre on a gap, so there are 2n − 1 centres in total.

approaches.title: Check substrings that could beat the best

idea.md: For each start `i`, test every end `j` that would give a longer palindrome than the best so far, with a two-pointer check.

build: Loop over starts and longer-than-best ends.
Keep the longest (first found on ties).

lines.text: A single letter is always a palindrome.
Only ends that would beat the current best need testing.
Two pointers from both ends of `s[i..j]`.

notes.c: The text version copies it into a new string.

complexity.md: **Time O(n³)** in the worst case. **Space O(1).**

walk.title: Check substrings from each start, longest-first candidates only: a substring is worth testing only if it would beat the best so far.

limits.md: Each substring is re-tested from its ends. Growing palindromes from their centres reuses the inner match.

idea.md: For each centre `c` (`i = c / 2`, `j = i + c % 2`), widen while `s[i] == s[j]`. The palindrome is `s[i+1..j−1]`; keep it if strictly longer than the best.

lines.text: The best so far: a single letter at position 0.
Widen while the ends match; afterwards the palindrome is `s[i+1..j−1]`, of length `j − i − 1`.
Strictly longer only, so earlier palindromes win ties (centres are visited left to right).

notes.c: The text version copies it into a new string.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** in the worst case. **Space O(1).**

steps.text: Centre at letter 0: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'x'.
Centre at letter 1: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'a'.
Centre at letter 2: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'b'.
Centre at gap 2.5: expands 2 step(s); the widest is 'abba'.
Centre at letter 3: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'b'.
Centre at letter 4: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'a'.
Centre at letter 5: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'y'.
Centre at letter 6: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'c'.
Centre at letter 7: expands 2 step(s); the widest is 'cdc'.
Centre at letter 8: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'c'.
Centre at letter 9: expands 1 step(s); the widest is 'z'.

walk.title: Expand around each of the 2n − 1 centres; the widest expansion wins (the earliest one on ties, since later ties don't replace it).

takeaways.md:
- **Longest palindromic substring = expand around 2n − 1 centres**, O(n²) and O(1) memory.
- Track the start and length, not the string, until the end.
- Manacher's algorithm does it in O(n) when n is large.
